analyzed_vuln.description: The duplicate-ID path mishandles an ID hash entry originally created in streaming mode. Streaming creation leaves `ret->attr == NULL`, but on a duplicate `xmlAddIDSafe` only assigns `ret->attr = attr` inside `if (ret->attr != NULL)`, while unconditionally assigning `attr->id = ret`. Consequently, successive duplicate attributes can all retain the same `xmlID *`. During malformed entity-tree cleanup, freeing one such attribute calls `xmlRemoveID`, removes the hash entry, and frees the shared `xmlID`; freeing the next attribute dereferences its dangling `attr->id` in `xmlRemoveID` at valid.c:2521, causing the heap-use-after-free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Parse through the XML reader/streaming path with a DTD-declared ID attribute and at least three occurrences of the same ID value in an expanded entity: the first creates a streaming `xmlID` with no owning attribute, and the next two duplicates both receive that same pointer. The PoV's malformed entity (`<dest id='foo'>` repeated three times and left incomplete) drives recovery cleanup of the temporary entity tree. Cleanup frees the first pointer-bearing duplicate and its hash entry, then frees another duplicate whose `attr->id` is dangling, triggering the UAF.

args: Analyze the duplicate-ID branch of xmlAddIDSafe in libxml2/valid.c at lines 2322-2333. What ownership invariant exists between xmlID::attr and xmlAttr::id, why does the code transfer ownership on duplicates for entities, and should the root fix move `ret->attr = attr` outside `if (ret->attr != NULL)` (while retaining clearing of the old attr only conditionally)? Please identify any nearby tests or call-path semantics relevant to streaming mode.

The ASan reproducer parses through xmlreader with a DTD ID and a malformed expanded entity containing the same ID three times. The initial streaming registration creates xmlID with ret->attr == NULL. On duplicates, current code conditionally clears the prior ret->attr and assigns ret->attr only if non-NULL, but unconditionally sets each duplicate attr->id = ret. Thus several attrs share one xmlID and cleanup frees it through one attr before dereferencing it through another. I have inspected xmlAddIDSafe at libxml2/valid.c:2295, xmlAddID at 2396, and xmlRemoveID at 2511. The likely minimal correction is `if (ret->attr != NULL) ret->attr->id = NULL; ret->attr = attr;`, maintaining exactly one owning backlink. I want confirmation of intended semantics and whether streaming duplicates should instead receive no backlink.
